name: biv_wall_ocs12_diseased

This is the approved wall the coupled runs use; it builds and meshes with all 384 annulus points imposed.

name: biv_wall_ocs13
title: OCS13: BiV wall (solid only, does not mesh yet)
description: Solid geometry, no mesh. Septal-aligned 3 mm build around the OCS13 annulus (307 points, black ring): ann_rz 122.2 deg, LV endo 32 mm, wedge height raised to 4.34 mm (--wedge-below-annulus 1.0) because this annulus dips 3.3 mm below its mean plane; healthy-size RVOT placement. The solid is complete, but imprinting the annulus points along about 7 mm next to the septum-trunk corner breaks the tet mesh (2026-11-13).
group: BiV walls from the OCS valves

name: biv_wall_ocs14
title: OCS14: BiV wall (solid only, does not mesh yet)

name: clip_rv4mmHg

name: septal_clip_rv4mmHg_midplane

name: clip_release_ocs14_damp1
title: OCS14 clip release, springs + damper (furthest run)
description: Run 44 w0.2_damp1 (standalone OCS14 valve + clip): pressurize, grasp, then from t 0.26 each clip body's zero-length spring to ground drops log-linearly from k 1e4 (factor 10 per 0.05 s) with a damper c 1 switched on. Clip drifts as one unit, no rotation: 0.13 mm at t 0.29, 1.0 mm at 0.33, 3.9 mm at 0.374. ERROR at t 0.377 (k about 46).

name: echo_tv_D-02-S-03-b_t0032
title: Baseline chordae (t0032)
description: Patient tricuspid valve D-02-S-03-b reconstructed from echo. 49 chordae to 3 papillary points, ventricular pressure ramped smoothly to 20 mmHg over 0-0.05 s then held to 0.1 s.

name: echo_tv_D-02-S-03-b_belly_col0PM4_clamped_p23
title: Belly chordae + PM4, clamped annulus, 23 mmHg (identification valve)
description: Patient tricuspid valve D-02-S-03-b from echo. Pareto trial 32 (49 free-edge chordae, 3 papillary points) plus 24 belly chordae and a 4th papillary point under commissure col 0 (82 chordae), annulus rotation clamped, pressure ramped smoothly to 23 mmHg over 0-0.05 s then held to 0.1 s. The geometry used for the (G, t) identification; this solve is the pipeline's uniform neo-Hookean leaflet at the box centre, G = 29.5 kPa, t = 0.6725 mm.

name: echo_tv_D-03-S-02_t0043_fan5_L3
title: Fan chordae (5 branches, 3 mm), trial 43
description: Patient tricuspid valve D-03-S-02 from echo, Pareto trial 43 chordae rebuilt as fans: each of the 49 chordae is a trunk from the papillary point to a free branch node 3 mm off the leaflet (original stiffness 15 mN/mm and slack kept) plus five branches (15 mN/mm each, no slack) into a 5-node patch centred one row in from the original free-edge node; effective chord stiffness 12.5 mN/mm. Free-edge element stretch drops from 1.51 median / 3.37 max to 1.11 / 1.42 (leaflet body 1.30); closure unchanged (open area 2.4 mm2). Pressure ramped smoothly to 20 mmHg over 0-0.05 s then held to 0.1 s, annulus pinned. Uniform neo-Hookean leaflet, G = 29.5 kPa, t = 0.6725 mm. Rods = trunks and branches.

name: echo_tv_D-03-S-02_t0043

name: biv_isovolumic_caps_At
title: BiV isovolumic contraction, fully active outflow wall (At)
description: Posterior caps. The RV outflow-tract wall contracts with the same T0 as the RV free wall. Fill to 4 mmHg, then FEBio's volume constraint holds the RV + outflow volume while the active stress T0 ramps until the cavity reaches 40 mmHg (frame 25 onward). T0 98 kPa at 40 mmHg (passive outflow wall: 203).

name: biv_isovolumic_caps_Ag
title: BiV isovolumic contraction, graded active outflow wall (Ag)
description: Posterior caps. The RV outflow-tract wall contracts with T0 x 1.0 at the RV border falling to x 0.5 at the pulmonary valve (6 bands). Fill to 4 mmHg, then FEBio's volume constraint holds the RV + outflow volume while the active stress T0 ramps until the cavity reaches 40 mmHg (frame 25 onward). T0 104 kPa at 40 mmHg (passive outflow wall: 203).

name: biv_isovolumic_caps_C2ft_LV8
title: BiV isovolumic contraction, spread chordae + fully active outflow wall, LV 8 mmHg (C2ft_LV8)
description: Posterior caps plus 97 zero-slack OCS12 chords from the PM tips to points spread over the tricuspid cap (681 rods). The RV outflow-tract wall contracts with the same T0 as the RV free wall; 8 mmHg in the LV (ramped with the fill, constant afterwards; LV wall passive). Fill to 4 mmHg (frames 0-24), then FEBio's volume constraint holds the RV + outflow volume while the active stress T0 ramps to 203 kPa (frames 24-48). Displacement only, no stress (the stress rerun is not finished). The cavity passes 40 mmHg near frame 35 (T0 89 kPa at 40 mmHg; graded outflow wall C2fg_LV8: 94) and ends at 79 mmHg. Volume held within 0.04 %.

name: ocs12_febio_vs_abaqus
title: OCS12 diseased: FEBio (left) vs Abaqus (right), PM pull then 5.666 kPa
description: Standalone OCS12 diseased valve, two solvers on one clock (t 0-0.07; Abaqus times mapped with abaqus_febio_time.vtk.series): PM pull 0-0.02, pressure ramp to 5.666 kPa plus annulus motion 0.02-0.04, hold 0.04-0.07. Left: FEBio, pins/valve_ocs12_abaqus_equiv in biv_valve_pipeline (variant r5_annulus_afterpm): round-5 calibrated chordae (97 springs), annulus following the Abaqus path. Right: Abaqus with its truss chordae, shifted 71.7 mm along x. The two apply the annulus motion in a different order (Abaqus moves the annulus partly during the PM pull, FEBio holds it during the pull and applies the whole motion with the pressure), so they coincide only at the end state. At the end, median leaflet distance to Abaqus is 0.86 / 1.04 / 0.89 mm (Posterior / Anterior / Septal). Stress: FEBio VTK stress vs Abaqus membrane stress (mean of top/bottom surface); end-state von Mises median P/A/S 83/73/59 kPa (FEBio) vs 95/85/76 kPa (Abaqus).
